text: {"v":1,"mode":"lesson","intent":"Explain why the daytime sky looks blue","scene":{"family":"drawing"},"steps":[{"caption":"Sunlight starts as a mixture of many visible colors, and the atmosphere contains tiny gas molecules.","draw":[{"op":"circle","center":[90,100],"radius":45,"id":"sun"},{"op":"label","target":"sun","text":"Sun"},{"op":"rect","origin":[240,40],"size":[180,220],"id":"air"},{"op":"label","target":"air","text":"Atmosphere"}]},{"caption":"As sunlight enters the atmosphere, gas molecules scatter the shorter blue wavelengths more strongly than the longer red wavelengths.","draw":[{"op":"arrow","from":[135,100],"to":[240,100],"id":"white-ray"},{"op":"label","target":"white-ray","text":"Sunlight"}]},{"caption":"Blue light is scattered in many directions, so blue light reaches your eyes from across the sky.","draw":[{"op":"arrow","from":[300,100],"to":[470,55],"id":"blue-up"},{"op":"arrow","from":[300,100],"to":[470,165],"id":"blue-side"},{"op":"arrow","from":[300,100],"to":[200,300],"id":"blue-view"},{"op":"label","target":"blue-up","text":"More blue light"}]}],"claims":[],"takeaway":"The sky looks blue because air molecules scatter blue light more efficiently than most other visible colors."}
